page: Microsoft Azure E64_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores via Intel Hyper-Threading, operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. It utilizes an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor based on the x86_64 architecture, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache. Architectural capabilities include hardware acceleration via AVX-512 foundation and VNNI extensions, AES cryptography, and bit manipulation instructions.

System memory totals 504.0 GB, establishing a high memory-to-vCPU allocation of 7.88 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring external network-attached volumes for data persistence and operating system storage. Hardware graphics acceleration is omitted with zero GPUs provisioned, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate solid throughput in memory-centric and vector computation tasks. In PassMark tests, the instance scored 2917.59 in the memory suite, 57590.48 in extended CPU instructions, and 22694.2 in database operations, all ranking in the upper quartile. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 254.85 GB/sec, also placing in the top quartile. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 178.84 GB/sec, while write operations measured 88.57 GB/sec. Conversely, CPU-based large language model generation throughput is weak, registering 41.9 tokens per second on small models and 6.55 tokens per second on medium models due to the absence of dedicated matrix or GPU accelerators.

The hardware configuration provides high density for memory-bound systems that do not mandate local disk caching. The high memory footprint supports enterprise relational database management systems, large in-memory caches, analytics engines, and data processing pipelines.
